newsitem.title: USA: Improved lease propsed to lure Seahawks buyer.
newsitem.headline: Improved lease propsed to lure Seahawks buyer.

text.p: A top county official Wednesday proposed offering Microsoft Corp co-founder Paul Allen improved stadium lease terms if the billionaire exercises his option to buy the Seattle Seahawks football team.

In a letter to county legislators, county executive Gary Locke proposed shortening the team's lease of the Kingdome to three years from 10 if Allen buys the team and agrees to keep it in the Seattle area.
Locke, who is a leading candidate to become the state's next governor, also said he would consider reducing the team's rent and increasing its share of advertising, concession and other revenues.

"It is obvious that professional football can no longer be healthy here under the current ownership of the Seahawks," Locke said. "I would strongly prefer that we spend our time and energy working with Mr. Allen rather than resuming the costly court battle against the current ownership."

Allen, who owns a portfolio of technology and entertainment companies and a Microsoft stake valued at nearly $7 billion, paid an estimated $20 million this year for an option to buy the team from real estate developer Ken Behring.

The move put on hold Behring's plans to move the team to southern California, which had been challenged in court by state and county officials. But Allen has said he wants "significant progress" toward a new or improved football facility if he is to buy the team before his option expires July 1, 1997.

Allen aides have been busy exploring options other than the Kingdome, including the possibility of renovating the University of Washington's Husky Stadium, which features a lake view and more seats than the dreary, 20-year-old Kingdome.
Locke said any change in the lease terms, which would require approval of the County Council, would be structured so it could not benefit Behring.
